criterion_1_global_divergence.instructions: Criterion 1, global divergence. Separate changes L and R to a base program B interfere when there is a state element x such that B, L and R compute pairwise different values for x. Using the base, left, right and merge versions and the declared change summaries, is there evidence of pairwise divergence among base, left and right? A textual or code difference alone is not C1. C1 is true only when the same concrete state element has pairwise different values in B, L and R. If B and R are equal and only L changed, answer false.

criteria.false: No state element is computed with pairwise different values by base, left and right.
criteria.true: At least one state element is computed with pairwise different values by base, left and right.

criterion_2_parent_change_loss.instructions: Criterion 2, lost parent change. Separate changes L and R to a base program B interfere when there is a state element x such that L (or R) computes a value different from both B and Merge for x, meaning that Merge fails to preserve a change made by a parent. Using the base, left, right and merge versions and the declared change summaries, is there evidence of a lost parent change? If Merge preserves the change made by L or R, C2 is false, even if the source text differs. C2 requires the parent's value to be lost from both B and Merge.

criteria.false: No state element shows a parent value that differs from both base and merge.
criteria.true: At least one state element shows a parent value that differs from both base and merge.

criterion_3_merge_new_effect.instructions: Criterion 3, unexpected merge effect. Separate changes L and R to a base program B interfere when there is a state element x such that B, L and R compute the same value for x, but Merge computes a different value. Equivalently, Merge has new effects besides the ones in L and R. Using the base, left, right and merge versions and the declared change summaries, is there evidence of an unexpected merge effect? If B, L and R are not all equal for the same state element, C3 is false. A merge-only textual addition is not enough.

criteria.false: No state element is unchanged in base, left and right while differing in merge.
criteria.true: At least one state element is unchanged in base, left and right while differing in merge.

T1.instructions: As mudanças de Left e Right podem interagir neste método?

criterion_1_global_divergence.instructions: Criterion 1, global divergence. Separate changes L and R to a base program B interfere when there is a state element x such that B, L and R compute pairwise different values for x. Using the base, left, right and merge versions and the declared change summaries, is there evidence of pairwise divergence among base, left and right? A textual or code difference alone is not C1. C1 is true only when the same concrete state element has pairwise different values in B, L and R. If B and R are equal and only L changed, answer false.

criteria.false: No state element is computed with pairwise different values by base, left and right.
criteria.true: At least one state element is computed with pairwise different values by base, left and right.

criterion_2_parent_change_loss.instructions: Criterion 2, lost parent change. Separate changes L and R to a base program B interfere when there is a state element x such that L (or R) computes a value different from both B and Merge for x, meaning that Merge fails to preserve a change made by a parent. Using the base, left, right and merge versions and the declared change summaries, is there evidence of a lost parent change? If Merge preserves the change made by L or R, C2 is false, even if the source text differs. C2 requires the parent's value to be lost from both B and Merge.

criteria.false: No state element shows a parent value that differs from both base and merge.
criteria.true: At least one state element shows a parent value that differs from both base and merge.

criterion_3_merge_new_effect.instructions: Criterion 3, unexpected merge effect. Separate changes L and R to a base program B interfere when there is a state element x such that B, L and R compute the same value for x, but Merge computes a different value. Equivalently, Merge has new effects besides the ones in L and R. Using the base, left, right and merge versions and the declared change summaries, is there evidence of an unexpected merge effect? If B, L and R are not all equal for the same state element, C3 is false. A merge-only textual addition is not enough.

criteria.false: No state element is unchanged in base, left and right while differing in merge.
criteria.true: At least one state element is unchanged in base, left and right while differing in merge.

witness_state_element.instructions: Which single concrete state element is the most plausible witness for a semantic difference among base, left, right and merge? If you cannot name a concrete state element, choose none.

primary_criterion.instructions: Which of the three interference criteria is most strongly suggested by the state? Choose exactly one. Choose 'none' only when none of the criteria is supported.

criteria.criterion_1_global_divergence: Criterion 1: Divergência global. Existe um state element x tal que B, L e R calculam valores diferentes entre si para x.
criteria.criterion_2_parent_change_loss: Criterion 2: Perda de alteração do pai. Existe um state element x tal que L (ou R) calcula um valor diferente de B e de Merge para x.
criteria.criterion_3_merge_new_effect: Criterion 3: Efeito colateral inesperado do merge. Existe um state element x tal que B, L e R calculam o mesmo valor para x, mas Merge calcula um valor diferente. De forma equivalente, Merge introduz novos efeitos além dos de L e R.
criteria.none: No interference criterion is supported by the available code and change summaries.
